name: Didier Domange
current_role: Chairman of the Supervisory Board, Fidoma SAS (Domange family holding); former Chairman of Zodiac Aerospace Supervisory Board
profile: Didier Domange is the Domange family patriarch, and the family was long Zodiac Aerospace's reference shareholder. He chaired Zodiac's Supervisory Board until Safran acquired the company in 2018. He then sat on Safran's board (2018-2022) and now runs the family holding Fidoma.
interesting_fact: After Safran bought Zodiac Aerospace for about EUR 10bn, Domange joined Safran's board of directors from 2018 to 2022. The family's stake became Safran shares.
notes: Very private and has almost no public profile. Insider-profile sites disagree on his dates. Alive status is unverified after his Safran board term ended in May 2022. Any route to him would go through Safran's corporate office, though Safran has no link to him today.

name: Mitchell Jacobson
current_role: Non-executive Chairman of the Board, MSC Industrial Direct Co. (MSC Industrial Supply), Melville, NY
profile: Mitchell Jacobson joined MSC, the industrial-supply distributor his father Sidney founded, in 1976. He became president in 1982 and CEO in 1995, and he took the company public that year. He stepped back as CEO in 2005 and has been non-executive chairman since 2013. He and his wife Kathy give through the Jacobson Family Foundation.
interesting_fact: MSC took its name from Manhattan Supply Company, a cutting-tool marketer his father bought in 1970. It grew into one of the largest industrial distributors in North America.
deep_cut_fact: He trained as a lawyer (Brandeis, then NYU Law) and worked at MSC on summers and holidays. When he joined full time in 1976, his first big project was a research tour of other industrial supply houses to find best practices to bring back to MSC.
notes: Low public profile. The published IR contact is Ryan Mills, VP Investor Relations. Avoid mentioning his parents' 2005 deaths.

name: Mike Lazaridis
current_role: Managing Partner & Co-Founder, Quantum Valley Investments (Waterloo, Ontario); founder of Perimeter Institute for Theoretical Physics
profile: Mike Lazaridis was born in Istanbul and grew up in Windsor, Ontario. He dropped out of the University of Waterloo in 1984 to found Research In Motion, the maker of the BlackBerry, and was co-CEO until 2012. He has since put hundreds of millions into Waterloo's quantum ecosystem: the Perimeter Institute, the Institute for Quantum Computing, and the $100M Quantum Valley Investments fund he co-founded with Doug Fregin.
interesting_fact: Before the BlackBerry, he won an Emmy (1994) and an Academy Award for Technical Achievement (1999) for a high-speed barcode reader used in film editing.
deep_cut_fact: At age 12 he won a prize from the Windsor Public Library for reading every science book in the library.
notes: Strong angle for an energy and data-center show: quantum computing and quantum-safe technology. Perimeter Institute marked its 25th anniversary in 2025, and he founded it. The library prize is cited on Wikipedia to an old CRN article, so verify it if possible.

name: Olivia Holding
current_role: President, E & F Properties Inc. and Twin States Farming Inc. (Smithfield, NC); President, Ella Ann L. & Frank B. Holding Foundation; major shareholder, First Citizens BancShares
profile: Olivia (Britton) Holding is one of four sisters of First Citizens chairman and CEO Frank Holding Jr. With her siblings she owns about 20% of First Citizens BancShares, the Raleigh bank her grandfather led from 1935. She runs the family's commercial-property and farming companies in Johnston County and the family foundation, and serves on North Carolina conservation and civic boards.
interesting_fact: Her family has run First Citizens since 1935. In 2023 the bank bought the collapsed Silicon Valley Bank, which turned it into a national player and put it on the Fortune 500.
deep_cut_fact: She once considered the Foreign Service but became an elementary-school guidance counselor (M.Ed., George Washington University, 1990), and later served as personnel director for YMCA Camp Seafarer. She sits on the boards of the NC Coastal Federation, NC Aquarium Society and the Research Triangle Park Foundation.
notes: Private passive shareholder, not a First Citizens executive. The bank's media address reaches the company, not her directly. Her environmental and coastal board work (NC Coastal Federation, EDF NC office) could be a hook for an energy show. Bio details date from a 2016 RTP profile.

name: Carson Brice
current_role: Major (10%+) shareholder, First Citizens BancShares (FCNCA); private individual, Raleigh, NC
profile: Carson Holding Brice is the youngest of the four sisters of Frank Holding Jr., chairman and CEO of Raleigh-based First Citizens Bank. With her siblings she owns about 20% of the bank and close to half the voting power, a stake from a family that has led the bank since 1935. SEC Form 4 filings show she is a passive holder who mostly makes gifts and trust transfers.
interesting_fact: The Holding family controls First Citizens, which acquired Silicon Valley Bank in 2023 and has since grown into a national bank on the Fortune 500.
notes: Very private and has almost no public profile beyond SEC filings. A UNC page says she is a UNC and UNC business school graduate (https://ie.unc.edu/people/f-bryan-brice-jr). The bank media address reaches the company, not her.

name: Phatanee Leksrisompong
current_role: Possibly Deputy Managing Director, Feed Technical/Academic Affairs, Charoen Pokphand Foods (CPF), as of 2020; unverified as the Hurun-listed person
profile: Hurun listed Phatanee Leksrisompong as a CP Group billionaire in 2018-2020, but no source found explains her stake or any link to the Chearavanont family. A CP veteran with this name (spelled Phatthanee) is a CPF deputy MD known as the group's first feed formulator. That person is likely, but not confirmed, to be the Hurun entry.
interesting_fact: A 2020 Thansettakij profile calls the CPF executive 'Khun Noi' the CP group's first feed formulator. It says she led development of iodine-enriched layer feed that raises egg iodine levels, and oversees about 900 staff.
deep_cut_fact: After a chemistry degree from Eastern Kentucky University, her first CP job was calculating feed formulas, at a time when the group brought in an analog computer (1975) for formula calculation.
notes: Identity is uncertain: confirm that the Hurun CP Group shareholder and the CPF feed executive are the same person before using the facts. She is not named among Dhanin Chearavanont's children. MarketScreener links her to CPF Poland. The contacts are CPF corporate addresses only.

name: Matthew Rabinowitz
current_role: Co-founder & Executive Chairman, Natera (NTRA); co-founder & chairman, MyOme
profile: Matthew Rabinowitz was born in Johannesburg and earned a Stanford PhD in electrical engineering. He co-founded Natera in 2004-05 after his sister's newborn died of a genetic condition, ran it as CEO until 2019, and took it public in 2015. He is now executive chairman of Natera and also chairs MyOme (whole-genome analysis) and Marble Therapeutics.
interesting_fact: He founded and chairs NatureEye, a drone-technology start-up that gives wildlife conservancies anti-poaching tools and new revenue models.
deep_cut_fact: Before genetics he worked on positioning. In 2000 he founded Rosum with GPS pioneers to fix location indoors using digital TV signals, co-authored a 2004 paper with GPS pioneer James Spilker, and won IEEE's 2006 Scott Helt Memorial Award. He also won South Africa's National Science Olympiad in 1990.
notes: Engineer turned founder with a strong technical story (GPS, then genomics). He told it on Sequoia's 'Crucible Moments' podcast (https://sequoiacap.com/podcast/crucible-moments-natera). Handle the family tragedy behind Natera with care.

name: Li Zhaonan
profile: Hurun China listed Li Zhaonan (李兆楠) from 2006 to 2013, and Hurun Global in 2014, with wealth attributed to 'Hengde' in insurance. Searches in English and Chinese found no reliable source that identifies the company or the person.
notes: He has not appeared on any list since 2014. Identity is unresolved: the 'Hengde' company could not be matched to a known insurer or holding company. A Chinese corporate registry (Qichacha/Tianyancha) would be needed to identify him. Low priority.

name: Geraldo Werninghaus
profile: Co-founder of WEG (founded 1961 in Jaraguá do Sul, Brazil, with Eggon João da Silva and Werner Ricardo Voigt), where he ran production. Died in a traffic accident on 10 February 1999. The 2014 Hurun entry presumably reflects his family's inherited WEG stake.
notes: Deceased in 1999 (source: https://www.weg.net/institutional/KG/en/history/founders). Living heirs include granddaughter Anne Werninghaus, described as WEG's largest heiress, and grandson Eduardo Werninghaus, CEO of WEG South Africa (https://www.nsctotal.com.br/?p=8014595). Research them separately if needed.

name: Daniel Dines
current_role: Co-founder, Chairman & CEO, UiPath (NYSE: PATH), New York
profile: Daniel Dines is a self-taught programmer from Onești, Romania. He started DeskOver in Bucharest in 2005 and built it into UiPath, the robotic-process-automation company that IPO'd on the NYSE in 2021. He handed the CEO job to Rob Enslin in early 2024 but returned as CEO in June 2024. He is now steering UiPath toward 'agentic' AI automation.
interesting_fact: Forbes dubbed him the 'Boss of the Bots', the first 'bot billionaire'. UiPath was bootstrapped in Bucharest for about a decade before raising venture money and became one of software's biggest IPOs.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding UiPath he spent 2000-2005 at Microsoft in Seattle, then went home to Bucharest to start DeskOver, a small outsourcing shop that became UiPath. In April 2019 he donated EUR 1 million to help rebuild Notre-Dame de Paris.
notes: Talks about his story readily: Sequoia 'Crucible Moments' episode and a 2019 Forbes cover. Good fit for an AI and automation angle. Avoid the 2019 layoffs.

name: Family Juffali
current_role: Family behind E. A. Juffali & Brothers (Jeddah); chairman Khaled bin Ahmed Al Juffali
profile: This 1996 Forbes entry covers the Juffali family of Saudi Arabia, owners of E. A. Juffali & Brothers. The Jeddah group was founded in 1946 and is one of the kingdom's largest private conglomerates, with about 59,000 employees, spanning Mercedes-Benz vehicles, power, construction, insurance and telecoms. The group is now chaired by Khaled Juffali.
interesting_fact: The Juffali group developed Saudi Arabia's first electricity generation and telecommunications, as well as early television concessions.
notes: A family, not an individual. Key earlier figures Ahmed Juffali (d. 1994) and Walid Juffali (d. 2016) are deceased. For outreach, research the chairman Khaled Juffali separately. The power-generation history fits an energy show.

name: Polys Haji-Ioannou
current_role: Founder/owner, Polyar Tankers; major shareholder, easyJet
profile: Polys Haji-Ioannou is the elder brother of easyJet founder Stelios and the son of Cypriot tanker magnate Loucas Haji-Ioannou (d. 2008). Much of his wealth comes from a large easyJet stake. He carries on the family shipping legacy with his own tanker fleet, Polyar Tankers, and invests in commercial and residential property in Cyprus, Greece, Monaco and London.
interesting_fact: His yacht 'Esmeralda' is named after one of the world's largest tortoises.
deep_cut_fact: His father Loucas, whose shipping business Polys continues, once owned the world's largest private tanker fleet, which he built up from the 1950s. Polys remains involved in the philanthropic foundation his father started.
notes: Do not confuse him with Polys V. Hajioannou, chairman and CEO of NYSE-listed Safe Bulkers and a relative from another branch of the family. Wikipedia currently merges the two, so check any Safe Bulkers claim before using it. Very private and based in Monaco. No published personal or office contact was found, and the web-search budget ran out before Polyar Tankers' site could be checked.

name: Xianbao Chen
current_role: Chairman & General Manager, Qiaqia Food Co. (ChaCha Food, SZSE: 002557), Hefei; controls parent Hefei Huatai Group
profile: Chen Xianbao was born in Hefei in 1959 and graduated from Wuxi Institute of Light Industry (now Jiangnan University) in 1982. He worked at a state-run Anhui sugar, tobacco and wine company before quitting in 1995 to found Huatai, which first sold ice pops. In 1999 he launched Qiaqia sunflower seeds, which became one of China's biggest snack-seed and nut brands; the company listed in Shenzhen in 2011.
interesting_fact: Qiaqia sales jumped from RMB 30m in its first year (1999) to RMB 1bn by 2006, helped by an early RMB 4m bet on CCTV advertising.
deep_cut_fact: The brand name 洽洽 comes from the cha-cha dance, and the 'water' radical in the character reflects his key product idea: boiling the seeds with herbal seasonings instead of roasting them, so they leave the eater's fingers clean.
notes: The input's SEC link (Gaotu Techedu CEO) is a name collision: Gaotu's CEO is Chen Xiangdong, not this person, so ignore it. The Qiaqia website (qiaqiafood.com) did not load. The SZSE investor-relations disclosures would be the route for an official contact.

name: Vineet Jain
current_role: Managing Director, Bennett, Coleman & Co. Ltd (The Times Group), India
profile: Vineet Jain was born in Kolkata in 1966 and is managing director of Bennett, Coleman & Co. (The Times Group), publisher of The Times of India and The Economic Times and owner of Times Now, and India's largest media group. He joined in 1987 and, with his elder brother Samir, built it into a print, TV, digital and entertainment conglomerate. He oversees the group's day-to-day entertainment and TV businesses.
interesting_fact: He is the great-grandson of Ramkrishna Dalmia, founder of The Times Group and the Dalmia Group. His grandfather Shanti Prasad Jain, father Ashok Jain and mother Indu Jain all chaired BCCL before him.
deep_cut_fact: He graduated from the American College of Switzerland before joining the family business in 1987. He received the Art Karat Award in 2018.
notes: He is the public face of the Times Group, while his brother Samir is reclusive. Ken Auletta's 2012 New Yorker profile 'Citizens Jain' is the definitive long read. No published personal or office contact was found, and the web-search budget ran out before the group's corporate contact pages could be checked. He is said to post on X, but the account was not verified.

name: Yasseen Mansour
current_role: Chairman, Palm Hills Developments (EGX: PHDC); shareholder, Mansour Group
profile: Yasseen Mansour is the youngest son of Loutfy Mansour, who founded Egypt's Mansour Group in 1952. The group is the exclusive distributor of GM vehicles and Caterpillar equipment in Egypt and several other countries and holds Egypt's McDonald's franchise. He shares ownership with his billionaire brothers Mohamed and Youssef. He co-founded the Mansour-Maghraby real-estate partnership and chairs Palm Hills Developments, one of Egypt's biggest real-estate developers.
interesting_fact: Mansour Group is the sole McDonald's franchisee in Egypt as well as the exclusive distributor of GM vehicles and Caterpillar equipment.
deep_cut_fact: A George Washington University graduate, he joined the family's Mansour Motors in 1986. He later co-founded Mansour & Maghraby Investment Development, a 60:40 venture with his cousin's Maghraby Group, which became majority owner of Palm Hills.
notes: The Palm Hills site has an online inquiry form but shows no published IR email. His Wikipedia page notes 2011 legal issues and the Suisse Secrets leak, so avoid those. Some reports have linked him to Al Ahly club leadership, but this was not verified, so check before mentioning.

name: Wang Aiguo
current_role: Chairman & CEO, Qingdao Gon Technology (国恩股份; SZSE 002768, HKEX-listed 2025); Chairman, Baotou Dongbao Bio-tech
profile: Wang Aiguo founded and runs Qingdao Gon Technology, a Qingdao group set up in December 2000 that makes modified and composite engineering plastics for home appliances, cars, electronics and new-energy uses. It listed in Shenzhen in 2015 and in Hong Kong in 2025. He also chairs Baotou Dongbao Bio-tech, a maker of gelatin, capsules and collagen, part of Gon's second 'big health' pillar.
interesting_fact: Gon runs on 'two wings': chemical new materials (including new-energy and display materials and artificial sports turf) and biomedical health (pharmaceutical gelatin, hollow capsules, collagen peptides).
notes: His name is very common and Chinese Wikipedia lists only unrelated people called 王爱国, so identify him by the company. No published email was found; the company's A-share and H-share investor-relations pages, linked from the site, are the formal route. The new-energy materials business is a possible angle for an energy show.
